responses.response: Probable error category: two separate issues, taxonomy plus FQN reference. Root cause: Container_WebUi is a guessed or wrongly cased kind that is not declared, and api is likely being referenced by short name instead of its full path. Verification step: first compare Container_WebUi against the exact shared kind names in the shared spec files, then inspect where the API element is declared and note its full FQN. Minimal fix: replace the guessed kind with the exact declared one, and reference the API by full FQN, for example system.api instead of api.

Probable error category: dynamic-view containment plus invalid layout hint. Root cause: system -> system.api models a parent calling its own child, which LikeC4 treats as the wrong interaction shape in a dynamic view, and rank same user, system.api is invalid because those elements are not siblings under the same parent context. Verification step: check the containment chain for system.api and compare the parents of user and system.api. Minimal fix: have the actor or an external peer call the child directly, for example user -> system.api Starts request, and remove the rank hint or replace it with a rank same only between true siblings.

Probable error category: both relationship taxonomy and broken FQN. Root cause: sends is not a declared logical relationship kind, and dataLayer.cache is likely not the real full path of the target element. Verification step: check the allowed model relationship kinds such as calls, async, reads, writes, and uses, and inspect the model hierarchy to confirm the cache element actual FQN. Minimal fix: choose the declared relationship kind that matches the intent, then use the real full FQN. A safe pattern is service -[uses]-> system.dataLayer.cache Uses cache; if the intent is messaging, use async instead.

Probable error category: wrong-scope relationship kind plus duplicated deployment traffic. Root cause: https was used as if it were a logical relationship type inside model, but protocol belongs in the relationship technology field, and the same app traffic was then redrawn between deployed instances even though deployment already inherits logical relationships through instanceOf. Verification step: confirm the failing line is in the logical model, then check whether the deployment apps already map back to model elements with instanceOf. Minimal fix: keep one logical relationship such as webapp -[calls]-> api Makes API requests with technology HTTPS and remove the duplicate app-to-app deployment edge; only keep deployment relationships that are truly deployment-specific.
